title: Stein connectedness for $\mathbf P^1_A$
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $Y_0=p^{-1}(V(I))$ as a subspace of $Y$, where $V(I)$ is the set of prime ideals containing $I$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In the Stein factorization [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization], $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the ring map $A\to B$ is integral (each element of $B$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$) and $(B,IB)$ is henselian. The space $Y$ is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space], $Y_0$ is closed, and every irreducible closed subset [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y$ meets $Y_0$ in a nonempty connected subset [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Consequently, for every Zariski sheaf of sets $F$ on $Y$ (a contravariant functor on its open subsets satisfying the sheaf gluing condition), restriction induces a bijection $\Gamma(Y,F)\to\Gamma(Y_0,i^{-1}F)$, where $i:Y_0\hookrightarrow Y$ is the inclusion and $i^{-1}F$ is the topological inverse image [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] with values in sets. The restriction map is the component on global sections of the adjunction unit $F\to i_*i^{-1}F$.

proof.text: Apply the general affine Stein factorization theorem to $p$. It gives integrality of $A\to B$. Apply integral extension of henselian pairs to obtain $(B,IB)$ henselian. No finiteness assertion is needed or inferred.

Properness means separated, finite type and universally closed. Over the affine spectrum the first two conditions give quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $Y$; the qcqs spectrality theorem then gives spectrality. The closed set $Y_0=p^{-1}(V(I))$ is closed: $V(I)$ is closed by the definition of the Zariski topology and a scheme morphism is continuous.

Fix a nonempty irreducible closed subset $C\subseteq Y$. Give it a closed subscheme structure $j:Z\to Y$ with image $C$. A closed immersion identifies its space with its image. The composite $p\circ j$ is proper, since closed immersions are proper and proper morphisms compose. Apply Stein factorization to this composite, obtaining $Z\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}D\xrightarrow{s}\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $A\to D$ integral, $q$ proper and all its fibres connected and nonempty.

Nonempty fibres make $q$ surjective. Its continuous image of the irreducible space $Z$ is therefore all of $\operatorname{Spec}D$, which is irreducible. The spectrum classification gives a prime $\mathfrak r$ with $V(\mathfrak r)=\operatorname{Spec}D$. Integral extension gives a henselian pair $(D,ID)$. The prime-connectedness lemma for this pair shows $V(\mathfrak r+ID)$ is nonempty connected. Since every prime of $D$ contains $\mathfrak r$, this set is exactly $V(ID)$.

The proper surjection $q$ is closed, by the definition of properness. It is a quotient map: if $q^{-1}(T)$ is closed, then $T=q(q^{-1}(T))$ is closed; the reverse direction is continuity. Its fibres are connected. Apply the connected-fibre quotient lemma to the closed connected set $V(ID)$, obtaining a nonempty connected preimage. For a prime $\mathfrak d$ of $D$, the inclusion $ID\subseteq\mathfrak d$ is equivalent to every image of an element of $I$ lying in $\mathfrak d$, hence to $I\subseteq s(\mathfrak d)$, since the spectrum map $s$ sends a prime to its contraction. Thus $q^{-1}(V(ID))=(p\circ j)^{-1}(V(I))$. Under the identification $Z\simeq C$, this is $C\cap Y_0$, proving the required intersection clause.

By step 2, $Y$ is spectral and $Y_0$ is closed. For any $y\in Y$, the closure $C=\overline{\{y\}}$ is nonempty, closed and irreducible: if $C=C_1\cup C_2$ with $C_i$ closed in $C$, each $C_i$ is closed in $Y$ because $C$ is closed, and then $y\in C_i$ for one $i$ and closedness forces $C\subseteq C_i$. Steps 3–5 therefore show $Y_0\cap\overline{\{y\}}$ is nonempty and connected for every $y$. Apply the spectral closed-restriction theorem (Tag 09ZG) to $X=Y$, $Z=Y_0$ and the arbitrary sheaf of sets $F$. Its conclusion is exactly bijectivity of the global-sections map of the unit $F\to i_*i^{-1}F$, using the topological inverse image with values in sets. No local constancy or constructibility condition on $F$ is used.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Every irreducible closed subset of $X$ meets $X_0$ in a connected nonempty
set. Consequently $\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_0,F_0)$ for every
Zariski sheaf $F$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Fix an irreducible closed subset and give it the reduced closed-subscheme
structure $C\subseteq X$. The map $C\to S$ is proper. Its Stein
factorization gives $C\xrightarrow{u}\operatorname{Spec}B \xrightarrow{v}S$, with $A\to B$ integral and $u$ having geometrically
connected fibres. Since $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian,
$(B,\mathfrak mB)$ is a henselian pair. The image
$D=v(\operatorname{Spec}B)$ is irreducible and closed because $C\to S$ is
proper. Henselian connectedness makes $D\cap V(\mathfrak m)$ connected and
nonempty. The map
$C\cap X_0\to D\cap V(\mathfrak m)$ is closed and surjective with connected
fibres, so the closed-surjection connected-fibre criterion makes
$C\cap X_0$ connected. This expands Tag
`0A0B`; the final equality of sections is Lemma
[lemma-weil-pbc-spectral-restriction].

**Status.** This statement is a conditional assembly: its two classical

this blueprint: (a) given that $A\to B$ is finite, the pair $(B,IB)$ is
henselian; (b) $Y$ is spectral and $Y_0$ is closed in $Y$; (c) hence the
Zariski restriction criterion applies to $(Y,Y_0)$. Outsourced to

affine henselian base; (ii) the connectedness input; (iii) the Zariski
comparison for the constructible sheaf occurring in the degree-zero argument,
which the locally constant form [lemma-weil-pbc-spectral-restriction] does not
supply.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let
$p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. In the Stein factorization
[def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization]

$$
  Y\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A,
$$

$A\to B$ is finite and $(B,IB)$ is henselian. Every irreducible closed subset
of $Y$ meets $Y_0$ in a nonempty connected subset. Therefore the Zariski
restriction criterion of [lemma-weil-pbc-spectral-restriction] applies to
$(Y,Y_0)$.

proof.text:
*Step 1 (finiteness).* The finiteness of $A\to B$ is not proved in this
blueprint; it is input (i) of [thm-weil-pbc-stein-inputs], where the
Noetherian reference and the approximation route available here are recorded.
We use it as a hypothesis for the rest of the proof.

*Step 2 (the pair $(B,IB)$ is henselian).* This is proved here. Given a
finite $B$-algebra $C$, the composite $A\to C$ is finite: finiteness is
closed under composition in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For such a $C$, every idempotent of $C/IC$
lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $C$, because $(A,I)$ is henselian
[def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and a finite $A$-algebra is in
particular integral over $A$. That is precisely the definition of the pair
$(B,IB)$ being henselian.

*Step 3 (connectedness).* This is not proved in this blueprint; it is input
(ii) of [thm-weil-pbc-stein-inputs], the henselian-pair proper-base-change
theorem stating that for $Z$ proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ every
irreducible closed subset of $Z$ meets $Z\times_AA/I$ in a nonempty connected
subset. Applied to $Z=Y$ it gives the connectedness clause of the statement.

*Step 4 (spectrality and closedness).* This is proved here. $Y$ is spectral
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]: $p$ is separated and of finite type, so
$Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the underlying space of a
scheme is sober with a basis of quasi-compact opens. The subscheme
$Y_0\subset Y$ is closed, since
$S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a closed immersion
and closed immersions are stable under base change by
[lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products].

*Step 5.* Steps 3 and 4 verify the hypotheses of the Zariski restriction
criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-spectral-restriction] for the pair $(Y,Y_0)$, so its
conclusion applies to $(Y,Y_0)$; the last assertion of the statement follows.
We repeat the warning of input (iii) of [thm-weil-pbc-stein-inputs]: that
criterion is available for *locally constant* sheaves only, and the
constructible sheaf to which the degree-zero argument applies it is not known
to be locally constant.

Fix an irreducible closed subset and give it the reduced closed-subscheme
structure $C\subseteq X$. The map $C\to S$ is proper. Its Stein
factorization gives $C\xrightarrow{u}\operatorname{Spec}B \xrightarrow{v}S$, with $A\to B$ integral and $u$ having geometrically
connected fibres. Since $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian,
$(B,\mathfrak mB)$ is a henselian pair. The image
$D=v(\operatorname{Spec}B)$ is irreducible and closed because $C\to S$ is
proper. Henselian connectedness makes $D\cap V(\mathfrak m)$ connected and
nonempty. The map
$C\cap X_0\to D\cap V(\mathfrak m)$ is closed and surjective with connected
fibres, so the closed-surjection connected-fibre criterion makes
$C\cap X_0$ connected. This expands Tag
`0A0B`; the final equality of sections is Lemma
[lemma-weil-pbc-spectral-restriction].
